title: Dmitry Solovyev
text:
Statistician | Data Scientist | Policy Analyst

About me
Hi there! If you landed (somehow) on this page, it means you’d like to know more about who I am.
My name is Dmitry, and I’m a data scientist with a background in public policy and statistics.
Right now, I work at TriMet, the public transit agency in Portland, Oregon, where I develop predictive models, design interactive dashboards, and support teams across planning, engineering, and customer experience. My work focuses on making sense of ridership patterns, testing service changes, and helping stakeholders understand what the data is really saying. I primarily use R and Python for my analysis and try to make sure that everyone could understand the results of my work no matter their background.
Originally from Russia, I have quite a diverse career path. Before TriMet, I spent nearly four years at Oregon State University. There, I completed two master’s degrees: one in Public Policy and another in Statistics, with an emphasis on biostatistics and experimental design. I also worked as a statistical consultant and teaching assistant, helping public health researchers design studies and analyze results, and teaching students how to approach real-world problems using data (to the best of my abilities).
Before moving to the US, I worked in public policy NGOs, where I built simulation models, evaluated large-scale interventions, and supported strategic decision-making in areas like healthcare, housing, and energy policy. I also obtained degrees in political science and international relations, so rest assured, there are topics to talk about on Friday evening with me.
Please feel free to hit me up with any questions. I’m still think about turning this page into some kind of mini-blog, and, who knows, I might do it one day.
If you are interested, there is also a small list of projects I worked on at some point - you can also go visit my github.

title: Projects

This interactive map displays bus stops and their corresponding routes, overlaid on a dynamic geographic interface. Users can click on bus stops to view detailed information such as stop name, served routes, and frequency. The map includes demographic overlay filters—such as age, income, race, and disability status—which can be adjusted to visualize how transit accessibility aligns with community characteristics. Filters dynamically update the map to highlight areas of interest and support equity-focused transit planning.


COVID-19 data quality analysis and their effect on policymaking

Source code
In this project, I developed an SIR model to predict COVID-19 incidence counts based on mortality data using the MCMC algorithm. After that, I evaluated model performance with time-series cross-validation and visualized training and validation results, and applied a synthetic control method to evaluate the effectiveness of policy interventions in addressing the pandemic.



Network Exploration of Maize Ds GFP Insertional Mutations

Source code
The purpose of the study is to explore the relationship between the maize protein protein interaction network and the fitness cost a genetic mutation. Specifically, this study explored the betweenness centrality, degree, and average neighbor degree of specific protein coding genes targeted in an unreleased prior dataset and study.



Reforms of Diplomatic Agencies in the Face of New Foreign Policy Challenges

Click to view
Analytical review of reforming diplomatic agencies based on the transformation experience of the diplomatic service in different countries over the past ten years. This review describes the global and national drivers of reforms, the details of their preparation and implementations, and the best practices applied by diplomatic agencies seeking to adapt to changing international foreign policies.



Russia’s COVID-19 Humanitarian Aid Dataset

Click to view
I developed and managed a comprehensive dataset on Russia’s COVID-19 humanitarian aid, conducted data validation and cleaning processes to ensure high-quality and reliable data for analysis and implemented an interactive dashboard to visualize and the distribution and impact of humanitarian aid.



Battleships Game Strategies Simulation

R code
Battleships a strategy-type guessing game for two players, played on ruled grids (paper or board) on which each player’s fleet of warships is marked. Before the start, players deploy their ships of different sizes on the grid, and the locations of the fleets are concealed from the other players. Players are trying to guess the location of enemy ships and hit them by taking turns. In this simulation project, I am investigating the most efficient ship placement strategies that would increase the chances of survival.
